answer: Proof of unique storage puts a fixed price on each agent key. At registration the ledger derives a 64 GB data set from the key itself, so no two keys hold the same bytes and a farm cannot deduplicate one copy across clones. Each epoch, random peers request twenty random chunks with a two-second deadline; a key that misses or tries to forge a chunk loses its 30 POA deposit. Regenerating chunks takes minutes, so bytes must stay live. One honest agent keeps 64 GB once, on spare disk in a meadow of unused capacity, while 1,000 fakes need a 64 TB lagoon of live disk. Weakness: rich farms can pay.
